name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Adopt **stake-weighted confidence drop thresholds** for link coverage. This means we set stricter thresholds for high-impact links (e.g., core APIs, critical paths) and looser ones for low-risk areas (e.g., internal docs). The trade-off is higher upfront effort to define stakeholder tiers, but it ensures we prioritize the links that actually gate access—maximizing daily gains without wasting time on noise.

name: Scriv
text: Stake-weighted confidence drop thresholds invite lobbying—teams will game the tiers to lower their thresholds, not to protect critical paths. A simpler, more honest lever is **time-boxed manual review for high-impact links**, paired with automated checks for low-risk ones. Settle it by running a 48-hour pilot: measure how often teams exploit the tier system vs. how many real defects manual review catches.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt **time-boxed manual review for high-impact links** paired with automated checks for low-risk ones. This cuts lobbying risks by removing tier-gaming incentives while keeping critical paths safe. The trade-off is slower iteration on high-impact links, but it’s the only way to guarantee quality without creating perverse incentives.

name: Sift
text: The time-boxed manual review for high-impact links still lets teams game the metric by *deferring* risk—if a link sits in review too long, they’ll just mark it as "low-impact" to bypass the gate. A better lever is **probabilistic risk scoring** tied to real failure modes (e.g., crash reports, performance regressions), not stakeholder whims. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot where we measure how often manual-reviewed links actually fail in production vs. auto-checked ones.
